title: Train at the Moving Edge: Rollout-Efficient RL for Large Reasoning Models
claim: Selecting high-utility training samples is a moving-target problem that static or costly prior selectors miss; ours tracks it cheaply and online.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: concept heatmap, prior-method comparison table, our pipeline; yes/no icons
description: Three colored panels read left to right. Panel A (orange) has a difficulty-versus-entropy heatmap with a dashed ellipse marking the learning edge where utility is highest. Below it, three timeline arrows (early, middle, later) show a bright segment drifting rightward. Panel B (purple) lists four prior selection strategies as mini pipelines with icons: prompt pool, sorting, rollout, filter, history buffer, auxiliary model. Each row has Online and Efficient columns marked with green checks, red crosses, or amber warnings, plus a short red limitation note. Panel C (teal) shows the proposed method as a vertical flow. It runs from a large prompt pool through Stage 1 coarse narrowing, a small candidate pool, and Stage 2 online verification to selected prompts and a rollout and GRPO update. A feedback loop refreshes the history buffer. A teal banner closes the panel.
caption: RLVR prompt selection is a moving-edge tracking problem. (A) Utility concentrates at intermediate difficulty and high uncertainty, and the learning edge is dynamic. (B) Prior methods face limitations in efficiently selecting online high-utility prompts. (C) HIVE combines history-informed coarse narrowing with low-cost online verification to track the current learning edge.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become essential for post-training large language models (LLMs) in reasoning tasks. While scaling rollouts can stabilize training and enhance performance, it introduces substantial computational overhead. In algorithms like GRPO, multiple rollouts per prompt incur prohibitive costs, as a large portion of prompts provide negligible gradients and are thus of low utility. This raises a key question: how to identify high-utility prompts before an expensive rollout? Our experimental analysis reveals that sample utility is non-uniform and dynamic: the strongest learning signals concentrate at the ``learning edge'', the intersection of intermediate difficulty and high response entropy, which shifts throughout training. Motivated by this observation, we propose HIVE, a history-informed and online-verified prompt selection framework for data-efficient RL training. HIVE first uses historical reward statistics and response entropy as a cheap prior to filter candidate prompts, and then employs prompt entropy as a real-time proxy to prune instances with stale utility. Across multiple reasoning benchmarks and base models, HIVE maintains reasoning accuracy with substantial rollout cost reduction, achieving up to 2.3× total training speedup.
